parts.context: A practice manager describes the layout and services of a new health centre.

transcript.text: Good evening, everyone, and thank you for coming to the opening evening of the Riverside Health Centre. I'm Dr Price, the practice manager, and I'd like to show you around the building using the plan on your handout.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: As you can see, there is just one entrance, at the bottom of the plan, and it leads straight to reception. We have designed it that way so that everyone, including people in wheelchairs, can come in without using stairs.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: Let's start with the area near the entrance. To the left of reception, on the same side as the front door, is the children's clinic. We made it colourful and quiet, because we know that young patients can be frightened.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: On the right of reception is a room for staff only, so please don't go in there. Now, if you go up from reception to the long corridor, you will find four rooms along the top of the building.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: If you look at the plan, you'll notice that the building has a very simple shape, which I think makes it easy to find your way around, even if you have never been here before.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: The first room at the far left end is the pharmacy. You can collect your medicine there after your appointment, and it will stay open until seven in the evening, which is later than the other rooms.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: Next to the pharmacy, the second room along, is the X-ray room. You can have a scan here without going to the hospital, which saves a lot of time, although the appointments must be booked by your doctor.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: The third room is the physiotherapy room. It has a large window looking over the river, and the therapists say patients feel calmer there. We hope it will help people recover from sports injuries.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: At the far right end of the corridor you'll find the blood test room. It's the busiest room in the morning, so if you can, come after eleven o'clock, when it's quieter.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: Now a few words about the appointments. You can book by telephone or online. If you book online, you'll receive a confirmation by text message within an hour, and you must show it at reception.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: If you cannot come, please cancel at least twenty-four hours before. Last year, nearly one in ten appointments at our old building were missed, and that means other patients waited longer.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: We also run free classes. On Tuesday evenings there is a stress management group, and on Thursday mornings there is a walking club, led by one of the nurses, which leaves from the front door.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: These classes are open to everyone who lives in the area, not only to patients of this practice, and they are completely free of charge, thanks to funding from the local council.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: Finally, if you need urgent help outside opening hours, please don't come here. Call the national helpline, which is open all night. The number is printed at the bottom of your handout.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE

transcript.text: Thank you again for coming. Please feel free to walk around the building now, and our nurses will be happy to answer any questions.
transcript.speaker: DR PRICE
